name: Holmes Chiropractic Care Gig Harbor Turkey Trot!
description:
Date of the Event- Thursday, Thanksgiving Morning!! 8am!

 

Thursday, Day of event registration price doubles to $60.

The event is timed by Tortoise & Hare Race Timing using RFID chips that are attached to your bib.  The event is using chip start technology, so don't worry about when you cross the start line as your time will begin when you cross.

 

Day Before Packet Pickup and T-Shirt/Socks purchase from 2-6 pm at the Gig Harbor United Methodist Church, 7400 Pioneer Way.

Shirts will be $20

Day of Event Packet Pickup and T-Shirt/Socks purchase starting at 7am Judson St (Starting Line).  

Shirts will be $20

 

Two cans (no glass jars) of food to be donated the day of the event only.

Proceeds of the event will benefit BackPack for kids, FISH Food bank, and Scholarships for High School Students entering college.

 

Parking: To avoid parking problems

 . Get there early

 . Check out "Gig Harbor Public Parking" map on webpage

 . Consider being dropped off

 . Share a ride

 . Schedule an Uber

NO DOGS ON COURSE PER CITY OF GIG HARBOR!

name: Hotfoot 5K Trail Run
description:
Mostly flat 5K Trail run/walk held at South Kitsap Regional Park.

The 24th running of the HotFoot 5K will be on Saturday June 20th, 2026.

Separate running of the 1 mile start is earlier at 0835. 5K start time is 0900. Awards are presented approximately 1010.

Registrations: Preregistration $25 for the 5K, $15 for the 1 mile, $35 Day of Race (DoR) Cash or Check Only

T-shirts available (separate cost) while supplies last; $25 pre, $30 DoR

Presented by South Kitsap Fire Rescue Volunteer Association

Proceeds benefit Community Scholarship and public 4th of July fireworks show.

COVID-19 requirements may apply: https://www.governor.wa.gov/sites/default/files/COVID19%20Racing%20Guidance.pdf 

Be prepared for COVID-9 updates

For more information, visit

name: I love the 90s 5k
description:
I love the 90s 5k! 🏃🏽‍♀️ 🏃🏽 

Get ready to groove and run down memory lane at the I Love the 90s 5K, where you can lace up your sneakers & jam to classic 90s tunes!

Join us for the I Love the 90s 5k! Lace up your sneakers and get ready to groove to the best hits of the 90s while running through beautiful Green Lake Park in Seattle, WA. This in-person event is a blast from the past, celebrating all things 90s. Whether you're a fan of grunge, pop, or hip-hop, this 5k is for you! Dress up in your favorite 90s attire and relive the nostalgia with fellow participants. The course will take you around the scenic Green Lake, providing a picturesque backdrop for your run. So grab your friends, put on your Walkman, and let's make some memories together at the I Love the 90s 5k!

Marathon: No shuttle to the start. You are responsible for your own transportation.

name: Jasper Mountain Trail Fest 2026
description:
Jasper Mountain Trail Fest is a fundraising event that benefits Jasper Mountain Reserve, an environmental 501(c)3 non-profit organization to improve and enhance wildlife habitats for rare and endangered flora and fauna native to the Blue Mountains in the Southeast corner of Washington State. Come and enjoy the beautiful natural scenery with the knowledge that your signup funds will benefit the conservation of the reserve.

 

For 2025, we are offering four unique race options:

1) Our classic (fifth annual!) 5-person relay race, 100 km total distance
2) Solo Half marathon, 13.1 miles with 2,570 feet of elevation gain
3) Solo Full marathon, 26.2 miles with 5,140 feet of elevation gain
4) Solo 7k Family Run (4.4 miles) with minimal elevation gain

 

Prices increases are on  April 17, 2025, May 18, 2025, and June 14, 2025. Sign up by May 29th, 2025 to guarantee you receive a race t-shirt and medal! (we have a few extras for late registrants on a first come-first serve basis).Contact info@jaspermountainreserve.org with any questions.

 

All races take place on the following single track trails (click on each for details):

Red Loop (3.3 miles)
Green Loop (4.4 miles)
Black Loop (5.4 miles)

 

Reserve Information and Accommodations

The start and finish line is at 934 Payne Hollow Road, Dayton, WA 99328, which can only be found on Google Maps.

 

Suggested arrival is during daylight the day prior to the race. Suggested departure is the day after the race. There will be an informal welcome reception and short presentation about the race in the Start/Finish area, commencing at 8:00PM on the evening prior to the race.

 

Parking and campsites, close to the start/finish line, is included in the race fee.

Campsites for racers are within Jasper Mountain Reserve. As this is a nature reserve, loud noises, including car engines, power generators, high volume loudspeakers etc. are strictly forbidden. Dogs must be on leash at all times. Camp-fires are only allowed at one designated area (please familiarize yourself with WA State and Columbia County seasonal camp fire restrictions). Bring your own food, water, and (battery) power sources (Jasper Mountain Reserve is off the grid, meaning there is no water or electricity). Portable sanitary facilities will be provided. As there is no garbage and recycling collection service please collect all trash and take it with you when you depart.

 

Accommodation options are also available just a short drive from the race! Choose from hotels and Airbnbs in nearby Dayton (11 miles from the event), Waitsburg (16 miles), or Walla Walla (37 miles).

 

Relay Race Details (Start Time 7:00AM):

Relay teams consist of 5 people sharing one assigned bib with an adjustable belt that can be exchanged between team members. Each racer signs up individually and can choose one of the following options:
1) No Team (the race organizers will assign you to a team)
2) Join an Existing Team
3) Create a New Team

 

All teams start together with the 1st runner of each team running the red loop at the same time. Once completed, the 1st runner passes the bib to the 2nd team member who will complete the green loop. Once completed, the 2nd team member passes the bib to the 3rd team member who will complete the black loop. Once completed, the 3rd team member passes on the bib to the 4th team member who will run the red loop, followed by the 5th team member who will run the green loop, followed by the 1st team member who will run the black loop and so on, until all 5 team members each have completed all three loops. Race timing will provide results for entire teams as well as individual times (splits) on each separate trail loop.

 

All three loops combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon. The relay race is expected to take 10-15 hours. Due to the rugged terrain which includes steep downhills, headlamps are mandatory for any runners after 8:00PM.

 

Half Marathon and Full Marathon Details (Start Time 7:00AM)

Calling all Ultra Trail Runners! Our new course is crafted specifically for the adventurous spirit of the ultra trail community. The half marathon is the perfect choice for those eager to test their limits or begin their journey toward ultra distances. For the fearless and bold, the full marathon awaits: 26.2 miles with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain, set against a backdrop of breathtaking natural beauty in the Blue Mountains. This isn't just a race; it’s a chance to immerse yourself in the beautiful landscape of a pristine nature reserve. Get ready to experience the ultimate trail running adventure, you won't be disappointed! All three trail loops within Jasper Mountain Reserve combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon, The full marathon will run the combined trail loops twice.

 

7k (4.4 miles) Family Run Details (Start Time 7:15AM)

This exciting new option will be on the beautiful Green Trail, 4.3 miles long with minimal elevation gain. It is ideal for runners who prefer a sprint option, or families with kids to run together, and for participants who prefer to walk.

Suggested arrival is during daylight the day prior to the race. Suggested departure is the day after the race. There will be an informal welcome reception and short presentation about the race in the Start/Finish area, commencing at 8:00PM on the evening prior to the race.

 

Parking and campsites, close to the start/finish line, is included in the race fee.

Campsites for racers are within Jasper Mountain Reserve. As this is a nature reserve, loud noises, including car engines, power generators, high volume loudspeakers etc. are strictly forbidden. Dogs must be on leash at all times. Camp-fires are only allowed at one designated area (please familiarize yourself with WA State and Columbia County seasonal camp fire restrictions). Bring your own food, water, and (battery) power sources (Jasper Mountain Reserve is off the grid, meaning there is no water or electricity). Portable sanitary facilities will be provided. As there is no garbage and recycling collection service please collect all trash and take it with you when you depart.

 

Accommodation options are also available just a short drive from the race! Choose from hotels and Airbnbs in nearby Dayton (11 miles from the event), Waitsburg (16 miles), or Walla Walla (37 miles).

 

Relay Race Details (Start Time 7:00AM):

Relay teams consist of 5 people sharing one assigned bib with an adjustable belt that can be exchanged between team members. Each racer signs up individually and can choose one of the following options:
1) No Team (the race organizers will assign you to a team)
2) Join an Existing Team
3) Create a New Team

 

All teams start together with the 1st runner of each team running the red loop at the same time. Once completed, the 1st runner passes the bib to the 2nd team member who will complete the green loop. Once completed, the 2nd team member passes the bib to the 3rd team member who will complete the black loop. Once completed, the 3rd team member passes on the bib to the 4th team member who will run the red loop, followed by the 5th team member who will run the green loop, followed by the 1st team member who will run the black loop and so on, until all 5 team members each have completed all three loops. Race timing will provide results for entire teams as well as individual times (splits) on each separate trail loop.

 

All three loops combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon. The relay race is expected to take 10-15 hours. Due to the rugged terrain which includes steep downhills, headlamps are mandatory for any runners after 8:00PM.

 

Half Marathon and Full Marathon Details (Start Time 7:00AM)

Calling all Ultra Trail Runners! Our new course is crafted specifically for the adventurous spirit of the ultra trail community. The half marathon is the perfect choice for those eager to test their limits or begin their journey toward ultra distances. For the fearless and bold, the full marathon awaits: 26.2 miles with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain, set against a backdrop of breathtaking natural beauty in the Blue Mountains. This isn't just a race; it’s a chance to immerse yourself in the beautiful landscape of a pristine nature reserve. Get ready to experience the ultimate trail running adventure, you won't be disappointed! All three trail loops within Jasper Mountain Reserve combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon, The full marathon will run the combined trail loops twice.

 

7k (4.4 miles) Family Run Details (Start Time 7:15AM)

This exciting new option will be on the beautiful Green Trail, 4.3 miles long with minimal elevation gain. It is ideal for runners who prefer a sprint option, or families with kids to run together, and for participants who prefer to walk.

description:

name: Jovita Strong 5K
description:
Support Jovita: Birthday 5K Run for Recovery

On Monday, April 28th, Jovita experienced a ruptured vein in her brain, resulting in significant bleeding. She was urgently transported to Harborview Medical Center, where she underwent emergency surgery.

Thanks to God’s grace and the incredible skill of her medical team, Jovita is now on the path to recovery. While the journey ahead will be long and challenging, her strength, resilience, and fighting spirit give us hope that her healing will be steady — and perhaps even faster than expected.

To support Jovita and her family during this time, we’re organizing a 5K run in celebration of her birthday, doing what she loved most: running the trail. All proceeds from the event will go directly to Jovita and her family to help cover the costs of her care.

Please join us in honoring Jovita’s spirit, celebrating her birthday, and showing our support through movement, community, and love.

name: Jumping Mouse Turkey Trot
description:

Family-friendly and dog-friendly atmosphere (strollers welcome too!)
An uplifting way to kick off the holiday season while giving back to kids in need
Let’s lace up, have fun, and make a difference together. 🦃💛

name: K is for Kindness 5 K and 1K Run
description:
K is for Kindness is a 5K and 1K fun run to benefit Spectrum Studios and Empower Center for Growth.  

The Tri-Cities only nonprofit for young adults on the autism spectrum who have aged out of school—creating opportunities, connections, enrichment and growth.

Empower Center for Growth is a welcoming community hub dedicated to individuals who are looking for a place to connect, learn, and grow. It’s a space to hang out with new friends, take creative and life-skills classes, and discover new interests in a supportive, inclusive environment. Whether you want to explore art, cooking, technology, or personal development, Empower Center for Growth is here to help you build confidence, friendships, and lifelong skills.

name: K9 Candy Cane 5K Fun Run
description:
The K9 Candy Cane 5K Fun Run and Walk is held at the Renton Community Center Campus. Runners and walkers travel along the paved beautiful Cedar River Trail before looping back to the Community Center Campus. Competitive runners, fun runners, walkers and families (with or without) dogs are all invited to this annual event. Accurate and professional chip timing is provided by Bell Lap Productions. If registered before 9:00AM on Wednesday, November 26, participants will receive a hooded sweatshirt. Don't forget about our Annual Pet Food Drive for furry friends in need, help us FILL THE TRUCK! 

Registration Windows:

  • Early Bird Registration - August 28 to November 1.
    • Guarantees you a hooded sweatshirt. 
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:        $20
    • Ages 18 and up fee:   $30
  • Standard Price Registration - November 2, ending at 9:00AM, November 26.
    • Guarantees you a hooded sweatshirt.  
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:       $30
    • Ages 18 and up fee:  $40
  • Last Chance Registration -  Begins 9:01AM November 26, through 1:00PM on Saturday December 6.
    • Not eligible to receive a hooded sweatshirt, Fun Run Only.
    • Ages 4 to 17 fee:       $30
    • Ages 18 and up fee:  $40

Race Bib Number Pick Up:
If you have pre-registered, you may pick up your race bib and sweatshirt (if applicable) at The Renton Community Center, 1715 Maple Valley Hwy. Renton, 98057, Saturday, December 6, 9:30AM – 5:00PM. If you are picking up for family members or friends, you will need their race day registration confirmation. You will also have the opportunity to pickup your race bib and sweatshirt onsite the morning of the race. 

Race Guidelines for Humans and Dogs:

  • Strollers are welcome on the course for both humans and dogs.
  • Participants NOT wanting to be timed should NOT pass through the finish line, please exit the course to the left or right prior to entering the timing chute.
  • Your race bib is your timing chip. Please wear it outside of your clothing facing forward for accurate timing.
  • Timing will conclude 45 minutes after the start of the race.
  • Walkers stay to the right of the race course.
  • Extra sweatshirts are NOT purchased and will NOT be available day of race.
  • No more than two dogs per person.
  • All dogs are required to be current on vaccinations.
  • No dogs under six months of age.
  • Dogs must be on leash no more than 6 feet in length.
  • Owners are responsible for the well-being and safety of their dog(s) at all times
  • No female dogs in heat. 
  • No aggressive dogs or aggressive owners. Any signs of aggression towards other dogs or participants will result in being asked to leave the event.
  • Owners are responsible for always picking up after their dog(s). 

Pet Food Drive:
Please bring a can/bag of pet food to be donated to local animals in need. Help us FILL THE TRUCK! 

Click here: Course Map

Course Closure:
Recreational walkers/runners are non-competitive and will not be timed if finishing after 45 minutes. If you are participating in this event but are not being timed please be considerate and not cross the finish line where timing is taking place. Keep to the right or left of the timing chute.

Awards and Results:
Awards will be given to the top three runners overall in female, male, non binary, and youth. Free event stickers will be included for all participants.

Hooded Sweatshirts:
After 9:00AM November 26, hooded Sweatshirts are no longer available. Extra sweatshirts are not purchased and will NOT be available at the end of the race. The sweatshirt size you selected is what's purchased. Sweatshirts are unisex sizing.

name: Lake Meridian Triathlon
description:

name: Lake Sammamish Half Marathon
description:
The Lake Sammamish Half Marathon is a point to point race that takes runners along the smooth trail that connects Marymoor Park in Redmond to Lake Sammamish State Park in Issaquah. This interurban trail is very popular with runners and is fully paved. We also offer a half-marathon walk category with a generous 4 hour time limit. This flat run is perfect for a half-marathon personal best whether you’re running or walking! 

The race is chip-timed, and each racer will receive a custom bib, participant shirt, and a finisher medal. Aid stations are provided every few miles (see course map) with Clif gels, Nuun and water, and the finish line will be by the beach and includes a nice line up of food and music.  

The Lake Sammamish Half is cupless, so you either need to bring a handheld bottle, wear a hydration pack, or we can provide you with a re-useable cup at the start line.

VIRTUAL RACE INFO - We have 40 spots for virtual runners. Once they sell out there are no more available. You can run the distance all at once or break it up into chunks and run it on the date of your choosing. You will receive a shirt and medal that will be mailed after the in person race.

Check out all the details on our website.

name: Lampson Cable Bridge Run
description:
This year marks the 47th annual running of the Lampson Cable Bridge Run! Finisher Medals will be given out to the first 2200 participants who finish the run. To receive your medal please ensure that your race bib is visible as you cross the finish line. So tell your friends and come out and enjoy this fun and exciting holiday tradition! Runners, no matter the distance they choose (5K or 10K) will start their race crossing over the Columbia River from Kennewick to Pasco, WA on the scenic Cable Bridge. The 1 mile runners will end shortly after crossing the bridge and be shuttled to the 5K/10K finish area. The 5K & 10K finish line is located at the Lampson warehouse. At the finish line you will receive your medal and refreshments before proceeding to catch the shuttle bus back to the fairground's parking lot. 

There is a discounted, non-timed 1 Mile Fun Run category for those that want to experience the fun and excitement of this yearly event, and still receive the finisher medal. Also there is a child 4 and under category that is free of charge. Participants in this category will receive their own special bib but will not be timed nor receive a finisher medal, instead they will receive a child's finisher ribbon.

For all timed race categories, timing chips are used and awards are given to the top participants in each age category. So if you are a competitive runner or someone who just wants to have fun walking with your friends, the Lampson Cable Bridge Run has what you are looking for.

name: Langlauf 10K XC Ski Race
description:
Langlauf is a 10K Cross Country Ski Race that takes place at the Mount Spokane Nordic Ski Center which is the premier Cross Country Ski Area in the Inland Northwest.  The race takes place on the traditional 10K course and has wave starts to accommodate skiers of all abilities and speeds.  Even maybe more epic than the race itself, are the pre and post race amenities that are enjoyed by all racers.  This is the biggest and oldest Cross Country Race in the Pacific Northwest...you don't want to miss it!

Once again, this year we are offering an adaptive skier category. If you are visually impaired or a sit skier you will be able to participate in our Wave start, but at Junction 1 will continue on Linder Road to a turnaround at the Inland gate then back to Brian's and our traditional finish line. Adaptive skiers must register but their guide skier can accompany them for no cost. Guides will need to sign a waiver the morning of the race and do not need to pay to register unless they want to be timed. Guides will be considered a volunteer and be entered in the prize drawing.

name: Last Chance Marathon and Half Marathon
description:
OK, here is your Last Chance to run a 1/2 marathon or full marathon this year! The 1/2 marathon course is an out and back and the full marathon course is the same out and back course two times, starting at Fairhaven Park Pavillion, running the Interurban trail out to Clayton Beach for the full 13.1 miles or 26.2. Course is subject to change if trail conditions mandate.

 

This trail has spectacular views and very few hills, just enough hills to make it interesting, and break up the flat sections. FYI: We have been known to have SNOW this time of the year so plan accordingly. The majority of this trail is covered with a canopy of trees which deflects some of the rain or snow, but this also means it doesn’t heat as fast as an open course would. It can get cold. The majority of the trail is an old railroad bed, very easy to run on gravel surface, with the exception of Arroyos Park. Arroyos Park is a double track trail with a few bridges and a few fun hills. It is a very well maintained set of trails.

 

The bathrooms at Fairhaven Park will be unlocked as well as the warm heated Pavillion.

 

You should plan on being self-sufficient and carrying your own water and aid. The 1st aid station on the course is ~ 3.5 miles into the race off Chuckanut Crest Drive. In the 1/2 marathon you will run by this aid station twice, and 4 times in the full marathon.  There will be an aid station at the turn around which you will access once in the 1/2 marathon and twice in the full marathon. We will also have an aid station at the start/finish so full 1/2 marathoners will have 3 chances to refill their water bottles, about every 3 to 3.5 miles, & marathoners will have 7 chances to refill their water bottles.  We will have water, an electrolyte drink and other snacks at the aid stations.  Usually I put some type of candy like candy corn, gummy bears, bananas, pretzels, typical ultra style foods. You won’t go hungry!
Keep an eye on the website for any changes to the event. Finishers will receive a Last Chance coin/medal similar to the quality of the Woolley Runs coin.  We will provide food at the end like all the NW Ultra Events.  While all your friends are recovering from their hang over and resting up before the evening’s festivities, you’ll be burning calories and ready to PARTY hardy knowing you’ve already burned off that extra beer or two, or three.

Additional details at the Leavenworth Firefighter Challenge web page.

name: Let Me Run Fall 5K 2025
description:
Come celebrate the end of season 5K for the Let Me Run program.  At Let Me Run we inspire boys through the power of running to be courageous enough to be themselves, to build healthy relationships, and to live an active lifestyle. This 5K celebrates 7 weeks of training for our boys and we invite you to join us as you walk, jog, or run to support the boys and help provide very important funding for our next season. This fall we are back at the beautiful course at Greenlake Park in Seattle.  Come feel the joy and sense of accomplishment as our boys cross the finish line!  

 

Schedule: 

8:30am - Registration and Packet Pickup opens

10:00am - 5K start 

10:45am - Awards

name: Light up the Night 5k
description:
Ring in the new year with sneakers, sparkles, and smiles! Our New Year’s Eve "Light up the Night 5K" isn’t about speed—it’s about celebration. Whether you're jogging, walking, skipping, or dancing your way through the course, you're guaranteed to end the year on a high note.

Everyone is encouraged to dress up—think glow sticks, LED tutus, silly hats, or even full-on costume sparkle! 

Families, kids, strollers, and pups on leashes are all welcome. This is your chance to do something active, social, and unforgettable before the clock strikes midnight.

Finish the year glowing—literally!  Come for the fun. Stay for the memories. And start the new year smiling.

name: Lookin For A Cure Seattle
description:
"We're "Lookin' For a Cure" in scenic Warren G Magnesun Park! Join A Cure In Sight on Saturday July 19th, 2025 from 8AM-11AM, to walk or run with us. We will be taking steps to find a cure for a rare eye cancer, Ocular Melanoma. Ocular Melanoma is estimated by the American Cancer Society to have roughly 3000 new cases each year nationwide. Bring your friends and family to the race day--all ages welcome to walk or run with us.

Register, become a fund raiser, make a team, grab your friends and family and raise money to support local research with Dr. Stacey and Fred Hutch Cancer Center.  Prizes will be awarded for largest team, largest fundraiser as well as top finishers.

Race Swag

  • Guarantee t-shirt if registered by June 30th.
  • Finisher Medal
  • Food & Drink
  • Aid Station
  • Commemorative Race Bib
  • Free downloadable photos
  • Official finishers time with age group placements

Race day schedule

  • Registration 7AM
  • Race start 8AM
  • Announcements Awards 10AM

Parking

Free parking past the boat launch area  just steps from the start line. If you have an issue on race day, please call 919-885-5264 for directions.

name: Lost Lake 25K
description:
Lost Lake 25K
Bellingham, Washington
Start: Lost Lake Trailhead
Finish: Larrabee State Park Amphitheater

Welcome to the Pacific Northwest’s hidden gem: the Lost Lake 25K — a perfectly crafted point-to-point trail run through the moss-draped forests, ridgelines, and  lake basins of Washington’s first state park.

This one-way loop (no redundancies, no backtracking) starts at the Lost Lake Trailhead, taking runners on a scenic journey through old-growth evergreens and fern-lined singletrack. The course weaves its way south through Larrabee’s rugged terrain, connecting some of the area’s most beautiful trails in a flowy, runnable rhythm.

On clear days, you’ll catch breathtaking views into Canada, over the bay into Bellingham, and across to the snow-capped summit of Mount Baker. Along the way, expect a mix of fast, forested descents, mellow climbs, and technical stretches near lakes and ridgelines.

The journey ends at the Larrabee State Park Amphitheater, where a celebratory finish line, post-race snacks, and mountain vibes await.

Whether you're chasing a PR or just soaking in the sights, this course delivers a little magic in every mile.

Come run the ridges, lakes, and lore of the Chuckanut Mountains. Welcome to Yeti.

name: Lunar New Year Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🏇🐎 Gallop Into the New Year! 🐎🏇
✨ Step into the Year of the Horse with purpose, energy, and community spirit! ✨
Celebrate culture, fitness, and fresh starts with the Lunar New Year’s Run, which is your chance to embrace the bold spirit of the horse - symbolizing energy, freedom, and forward momentum.

 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Maple Valley Bear Run & Walk 5K
description:
SCHEDULE FOR RACE DAY, 6/27/2026

7:30am - 8:30am   Packet pick up and day-of registration*
9:00am                  5K race starts
10:00am                Awards
*Day-of registration (until 8:30am) using your personal mobile device, then come pick up your bib from us! No on-site payments will be accepted.

 

RACE COURSE

USATF Certified Course!
5K Run/Walk Race Course map
 

PARKING

Parking will be available at Lake Wilderness Park. We highly encourage carpooling with others. Arrive early so you have enough time before race start!
Please see attached map for specifics. Parking and Race Day Map

 

PRE-RACE PACKET PICK UP

Pre-race packet pick up will be offered at Road Runner Sports in Kent Thursday, June 25, 2026 from 4-7pm.  Come and get your race bib and t-shirt* before the race.  Grab all of your race day needs when you come in to grab your race bib!  Join the VIP Family and get $10 in Rewards Cash to use on your purchase that day. ​If you are already a VIP Family Member, earn DOUBLE REWARDS on today's purchases.  Visit RoadRunnerSports.com today!
*T-shirts only guaranteed for those who register by May 31st.
 

CHIP TIMING

Chip timing will be provided by Tortoise and Hare Timing. Disposable chips will be placed on back of bib numbers. 

 

AWARDS

1st place in each age division wins the coveted Bear Run Bear! 
2nd-3rd place in each age division receive Bear Run Bells
Special awards for top 3 overall men and women will be based on gun time.

 

RACE RESULTS

Official race results will be posted on our website and online at Tortoise & Hare Timing.  Results will be based on chip time (crossing start line to crossing finish line).

 

STROLLERS, DOGS & WATER

We encourage the use of jogging strollers along the trails of this family-friendly 5K!  Out of consideration for other participants, dogs will not be allowed on the course (with the exception of service dogs). We do offer water at the end of the race.

 

GIVING BACK TO THE COMMUNITY 

Proceeds from the Bear Run will benefit Tahoma High School distance running programs administered by the Tahoma Cross Country Running Club.  The funds fill a wide range of needs for our large team of athletes including support for athletes and families who need help with team participation and summer camp fees, multiple scholarships awarded each year, and travel expenses beyond that available from the school district budget.  These kids work hard and run hard all year while maintaining exceptional grade point averages.  They deserve our support!

name: Maple Valley Turkey Trot: Thanksgiving Day 5K
description:
Join us for the 7th Annual Maple Valley Turkey Trot 5K presented by Cayce Grove Law Offices benefiting the Maple Valley Food Bank! Register by end of day November 1 to guarantee your race day t-shirt. Sign ups after November 1 do not guarantee a shirt.
___

The Maple Valley Turkey Trot is a FUN walk or trot Thanksgiving morning through Lake Wilderness Park organized with the intention of coming together as a community during the Thanksgiving holiday to help those in need.

Children in strollers are not required to register (but will not receive shirts). All proceeds raised will go to fund Maple Valley Food Bank Programs as we enter into our organization's busiest season. All ages are welcome! We encourage Thanksgiving costumes & accessories!
___

Thank you to all of our sponsors, for making this great community event possible!

 

PRESENTING SPONSOR

North East Landscaping Services

 

GOLD LEVEL SPONSORS

ACI - Active Construction Inc.

Columbia Bank

Maple Valley Shell and Fine Wine

Washington Auto Law

 

SILVER LEVEL SPONSORS

Lakeside Industries, Inc.

Molina Healthcare

SB Concrete

Silver Streak Trucking, Inc.

 

BRONZE LEVEL SPONSORS

Edward Jones, Maple Valley

Johnson's Home and Garden

New Community Church

Ryan Armstrong, John L. Scott Real Estate

Tahoma Education Association

Wilderness Animal Hospital

 

Interested in Sponsoring the Turkey Trot? Email carl@maplevalleyfoodbank.org

___

Advanced Packet Pickup
TBD!

Day-Of Schedule
- Packet pick-up will begin at 7:30 AM on race day. Come early to grab coffee and snacks, and take photos in our photo booth (and with our giant turkey)! There's plenty to do and we'll have music keep up the energy!
- The race will begin at the Beach House at Lake Wilderness Park promptly at 9:00.
- Race route: https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6296717431

Parking
Please utilize the lower parking lots at the Lake Wilderness Lodge, nearest the arboretum, or the park parking lots specifically. Upper lots near the lodge will be closed off for safety on the route.

Chip Timing
This event will NOT be timed. A fun-run in its fullest form!

Strollers, Dogs, Bikes, and Water
We encourage the use of jogging strollers along the route of this family-friendly 5K. However, out of consideration for other participants, dogs will not be allowed on the course (with the exception of service dogs). For the safety and convenience of all participants, bikes are NOT permitted, as this is a fairly narrow out and back course. We will have water stations near the beach house before and after the race.

Accessibility
Please note that, while generally flat, this race course may not be suitable for all abilities, as the terrain is both paved and gravel. There is a slight incline to access the Green to Cedar River Trail from the arboretum. We will have volunteers stationed at these points to assist on an as-needed basis.

___
Race Contact Info
If you have any additional questions about this race, please contact Jon Cantalini at info@maplevalleyfoodbank.org 

Tickets are non-transferable and non-refundable.

name: May the Course be with You 5k
description:
Get ready for a galaxy-sized adventure! May the 4th is more than just a day – it's a celebration of all things Star Wars! 🚀✨

This year, we’re inviting you to channel your inner Jedi (or Sith!) and join us for a FUN-tastic 5K race. Whether you're aiming to out-speed the Millennium Falcon or just looking for a fun day out, this race is for everyone. So, grab your lightsaber, throw on your favorite Star Wars outfit (Yoda ears? Wookiee costume? You name it!), and let's make this event truly legendary. 🏃‍♂️💨💫
Let the Force guide you as you race through the course with your friends. Whether you're a pro or just in it for the fun, the May the Course Be With You 5K promises plenty of laughs, surprises, and of course, a lot of galactic fun! 💥
DID YOU KNOW? May 4th has officially become Star Wars Day, thanks to the famous line “May the Force be with you” from Star Wars: A New Hope (1977). Since then, it's been echoed across films, books, and video games, becoming a day of celebration for fans around the galaxy. 🌌🎉
Ready to race? Don't forget to dress in your best Star Wars gear and bring your A-game – the Force will definitely be with you!
Check out our FAQs for all the details: May the Course Be With You 5K FAQs 🌠
May the course—and the fun—be with you! 🎉

name: McKenzie Mott Memorial Turkey Trot
description:
After the tragic loss of our 15 year old daughter the family tradition of getting together for a movie, thanksgiving dinner and lots of family time was so hard to face without her. Kenzie loved tradition so to help us honor her legacy we created a new tradition for our family. Our family friends "the Larsen's"  inspired us to do something Kenzie would love to do so we did, we ran! We were so blessed to have over fifty of our friends and family join us for our first race as well as overwhelmed by the monetary donation that helped support our Safe Driving Scholarship for all local High School seniors. This is our 10th annual race and all proceeds continue to fund our scholarships.

Race Check-in/ Shirt Pick Up -Nov 24th-Selkirk Middle School 5:30-7:00, Nov 25th- Selkirk Middle School 5:30-7:00 & Race Day Nov 27th 7:30 a.m.- 8:45 a.m. 

Selkirk Middle School-1409 N. Harvest PKWY, Liberty Lake, WA 99019

Race will start promptly at 9:00 a.m. NE corner of pavilion park. Parking is available at Liberty Lake Elementary and Liberty Creek Elementary.

*To guarantee a shirt size, register by November 10th.

name: Memorial Day Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
Honor, Remember, and Run for Freedom This Memorial Day, join us for the Memorial Day Freedom Run - a special event that combines a run with the powerful spirit of remembrance.  Whether you're running solo or with friends and family, this event honors the brave men and women who have sacrificed for our freedom.
Every mile you complete is a tribute to their courage and service.  With scenic routes, motivating challenges, and a community united in purpose, the Memorial Day Freedom Run is more than just a race - it's a meaningful way to pay respect while staying active. 
Sign up today to celebrate freedom, remember our heroes, and run for a cause that matters.  Together, we can make this Memorial Day unforgettable.

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Meridian Turkey Trot Fun Run
description:
Whether you walk, jog, or run, join us for a Turkey Trot at Bellewood Farms to help raise funds for the Meridian High School Cross Country Team!  Try to keep up with our speedy cross country team if you can or just trot along for some fun!  Costumes are encouraged for this fun, family-friendly event. 

Rain or shine, the race will be on.  It's a guaranteed fun time!

*Strollers built for trail running are invited along for the ride, however our furry friends will have to sit this one out.

Bellewood Farms
6140 Guide Meridian Rd., Lynden, WA

9:00am:    Bib pickup

             Day of event - $20 per person or $50 per family

name: Millwood Daze 5k
description:
Community celebration 5k favorite is back!  The Millwood Daze 5k returns this year.  From it's tree-lined start in historic Millwood, its a flat, fast loop course great for runners and walkers.  Join us for the Millwood Daze celebration after the run with a pancake breakfast, street fair with community booths, and a classic car show.

Tee shirts available for purchase to all registrants.  Order by 8/12 to have it by race day.  After that, tee shirt pick up or delivery will be arranged.

name: Moses Lake Turkey Trot
description:
Location Information
Blue Heron Park (start/finish boat launch area)
111 Westshore Drive
Moses Lake, WA 98837


About This Event
All proceeds benefit the Columbia Basin Cancer Foundation. You may donate extra if you would like during the registration process! If donating a large amount please contact Kelsie Eddie or mail to Columbia Basin Cancer Foundation at 1031 W. Broadway Ave to reduce amount you will pay in processing fees. Please label donations for Turkey Trot. We appreciate your support so much!!!!! Thank you! Must come to event to receive your event shirt. T-shirts given to ONLY early bird registrants. Last day for Early Bird pricing and shirts is November 15.

Event Registration Fees
Early Bird Registration Price (Last day - November 15): $25 + online registration fee + shirt

Late Registration (Starting November 16): $35 + registration fee (will NOT receive a shirt-extras given out after awards)

You may register online until 8:45am day of event for $35+registration fee but will NOT receive a shirt (Last day for shirts is November 15) must register online with own cell phone/device morning at race.

NO REFUNDS

AGE GROUP: Male and Female - 6 and under, 7-10, 11-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, and 70+; STROLLER DIVISION - Male and Female (runner receives award only)
ATTENTION! STROLLER DIVISION: If you register yourself in the stroller division then the runner will receive a shirt, time and medal if placed. The child will only receive a shirt if purchased during registration. It will cost an extra $15 to pay for the child's shirt. CHILDREN IN STROLLERS: Please do not sign up your child that will be in the stroller (you may buy extra tshirt if you would like) - This will mess with results for those 6 and under that will actually be running on their own. Thank you! 

Event Schedule
Day of event Packet Pickup - Blue Heron Park before event from 8am to 8:45am. Race begins at 9:00am. Awards about 10:00-10:15am. If you are unable to stay for award ceremony then check this website and Moses Lake Turkey Trot Facebook page for location and time of pickup. 

 

THANK YOU TO OUR LOCAL SPONSORS!

 

*RNH FARMS *

Premier Health Women's Wellness and Obstetrics

Pella Inland Northwest,Inc.

Telos Endeavors, Confluence Health, Samaritan Healthcare, O'Snap Photography, Weber Farms, Odegaard Farms

Cascade Natural Gas, Basin Conex, LTI, Inc, Miller's Fine Jewelers, Insta Stor, Calbom & Schwab Law Group, Insta Stor, Shirt Builders, Moses Lake Sports Physical Therapy, CC McGraw LLC
Ernie's Quality Meats and Wine, Kersey Family

name: My Better Half Marathon
description:
Prepare yourself for a running event like no other. Romance. Kitsch. Sweat. My Better Half Marathon is a celebration of running, romance and rom-coms. There are 4 categories: Bromance (two guy friends), Besties (two best friends), Lovers (romantically involved) and Lonely Hearts (self-explanatory). Join Orca Running, February 8th, 2026 as we celebrate love in all of its forms!

Lover's registration is for couples of all kinds! Bestie's registration is for two girlfriends, mom and daughter, guy and gal, or anyone you call your bestie. Bromance registration is for two dudes who probably don't want to admit that they're inseparable. Lonely Heart's registration is for those currently enjoying being single or looking for love.

The half marathon course is a total of 2 laps.  The first lap has a steep but quick hill early on and is 6.9 miles in length.  The second lap is 6.2 miles long and is nice and flat! The 10K course is a total of 2 laps.  The first lap has some hills in the beginning and is 3.7 miles long whereas the second lap is nice and flat and is 2.5 miles in length! The 5k course is 3.1 miles long.  A steep but quick hill in the beginning is a great warm-up but once you come back down it’s a breeze!

Half Marathon Relay: The relay course can be completed in any way you prefer, as long as both laps are completed.  Lap one is 6.9 miles long and has a quick but steep hill in the beginning, Lap two is 6.2 miles long and is nice and flat!  It doesn’t matter who completes which lap.  There is a relay hand off area just before the finish line (in the park gazebo) where you make the exchange from one runner to the other.

Your entry comes with long sleeve 1/4 zip shirt, finisher medal, hot post oatmeal, and free race photos!

The My Better Half Marathon supports Rebuilding Seattle Together.

name: Never Say Never Half Marathon & 10K
description:
This race is all about YOU! Every decision we make has YOU in mind. This is a race designed for everyone from first timers to seasoned racers to all of those in-between. It is a picturesque course with one sizable hill around mile 2 followed by flat road for the rest of the 10K and rolling hills for the remainder of the Half Marathon.  
There will be NINE water stations this year. There are six bathroom opportunities, and lots of fans cheering you on along the way. 
We are again partnering with BOX, a nonprofit organization founded by women, dedicated to building connections that support women and girls. In 2021 we donated $4,100 to the Highland School District, in 2022 we donated $2,000 plus products to Davis High School, in 2023 we presented a $3,000 check to Rod’s House plus a ton of period products, and in 2024 we were beyond proud to write an $8,300 to Children's Village. This was our biggest donation by far!!!! This year we are proud to announce we raised $9,000 for Yakima's YWCA!
We have finally decided on who we will be raising money for in 2026. We are so excited and proud to announce we will be raising money for Nathan's Place. When we started this crazy dream we raised money for Highland High School (unfortunately we did not have a race that year because of smoke) so, as this is our last year putting on the Never Say Never we wanted to again raise money for our hometown. 
Nathan's Place was born just last year!  Some amazing members of our community who noticed that our high school kids have no place to hang out after school dedicated their time and resources to create a gathering place. They have been worked tirelessly to make Nathan's Place more than just a dream. This summer they had work parties to paint and fix up a building the city was not using, they got their 501(c)3 status so they could raise money to get computers, games, a BBQ, a TV, and more. The kids were pumped to start the school year with a place to hang out, do homework, and give back to our community. Then an unfortunate accident happened this summer and the building got severely damaged. Currently they do not know if insurance will cover the cost of fixing the building so now Nathan's Place, has no place. They need our help more than ever. We don't want to see this dream, that our kids so badly need, go away. Your donations this year are going to make the biggest difference yet!
Flying pig trophies will be back again for first, second, and third place women and men runners and walkers for the Half Marathon and the 10K. 
However, if even a 10K doesn’t sound fun come for the Finish Line Celebration Party! This is FREE to attend and welcome to all! Come cheer on the racers, get fabulous grub from Tacos Don Chayo, get refreshed with local beverages, play yard games with or without your kids and partake in our BEST raffle yet! And the WHEEL of FUN will be back again for even more prizes!

name: North Olympic Discovery Marathon (5K / 10K/ Half / Full / Relay / Kids Marathon)
description:
The North Olympic Discovery Marathon, Marathon Walk, Marathon Relay and Half Marathon take place on a unique point to point course that incorporates the beautiful Olympic Discovery Trail with stunning views of the Olympic Mountains and a five mile finishing stretch along the shores of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. The 10K,  5K and Kids Marathon are an out-and-back along the shores of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. 

Frequent sightings of seals, eagles, and an array of shore birds are common from the trail. Iconic trestle bridges provide beautiful back drops. Salmon can be seen spawning at the Morse Creek crossing in the fall. The North Olympic Discovery Marathon is truly one of the most beautiful marathon venues anywhere.

This rails to trails course is a wide, hard surface (99% paved) trail. The course is marked at every mile and water stations are located approximately every two miles. Cool June weather can be expected  – average high is 65F, average low is 49F, average mean is 57F.

The race is organized by the Port Angeles Marathon Association – a group of accomplished amateur athletes.

The Marathon is a USATF certified course and a Boston Marathon qualifier.

name: OAT Run
description:
* 50K * Half Marathon * 12K *

The Olympic Adventure Trail Run (OAT Run) is a point-to-point trail 12K and half marathon as well as an out-and-back 50K that traverses Kelly Ridge between the Olympic National Park and the Strait of Juan de Fuca in Washington State, all on single-track trail.  Limit 130 runners per distance.

The OAT Run Experience

OAT Run is for trail runners who enjoy lush green forests filled with moss and ferns, towering evergreens, and spring trailside flowers. Runners will get a stunning view of the Elwha River Valley as they run by the “Living Room”. And if this wasn’t epic enough, get ready to eat, drink, and relax post-race with an amazing view of the Olympic Mountains. The after-party at Extreme Sports Park is a fun atmosphere, and racers will get hot burritos from Little Devil's Lunchbox and cold drinks, a toasty campfire, and door prizes (woot!). There will be a beer garden at the after-party as well, with proceeds to support 4PA, a local non-profit organization. 

What’s included?

In addition to an epic outdoor experience in the far northwest corner, all runners receive a professional well-organized event, a well-marked course, hydration and snacks at water stations along the course, a great piece of custom race swag, shuttle to start (and return shuttle back to parking area / party), chip timing, race photos, and after-party at Extreme Sports Park including a hot meal and a chance to win great door prizes from our local retailers. 

Bring cash or card as there will be a beer garden at the finish line, hosted by and benefitting local non-profit organization 4PA. 

This race sells out every year, so don't delay registering!

Giving Back

This race is a friendly, community-based event, and a portion of race proceeds is donated to the Peninsula Trails Coalition (Olympic Discovery Trail) and the Peninsula Chapter of the Back Country Horsemen of Washington, in appreciation for their countless hours of trail construction and maintenance on the North Olympic Peninsula.

Where to stay
Olympic Lodge in Port Angeles is offering a special 25% off discount for OAT Runners.
Booking link here. 
Or phone direct at 360-452-2993 and use booking code OAT to receive the same discounted pricing.

REFUND POLICY:
  • 50% refund available until March 15, NO REFUNDS AFTER THIS DATE. No deferrals to another race or next year's race.
  • You will have the choice during the registration process to buy cancellation insurance (unavailable for Canadian racers 
     - rules of the insurance company and not us or RunSignUp). With the insurance, you will get a full refund in certain circumstances including accident, illness and family emergency, even after the March 15th date. Here are details and FAQ about the RegShield insurance.
  • Transfers are allowed until 3 days before the race  Transfer instructions.
  • No deferrals
  • If we are forced to cancel for any reason, runners will get a free transfer to the next year, or an 80% refund

name: Oktoberfest Fly Away 10K Run & 5K Run/Walk
description:
Register Now for the 7th Annual Fly Away Run

Join us in 2026 for the 7th Annual Fly Away Run, a family-friendly community event featuring both a 5K run/walk and a 10K run. The race will begin in Kenmore and follow a marked course along the Burke-Gilman Trail toward Bothell.

Additional event details, including schedule, packet pickup information, and race-day amenities, will be shared as the event approaches.

The Fly Away Run is part of Kenmore’s Oktoberfest celebration, now in its 3rd year, bringing even more energy and excitement to this annual tradition.

 

2026 Day of Event Schedule - 

The Fly Away Run launches from the Burke-Gilman Trail access point in Kenmore, located at 192 Brewing Co. Lake Trail Taproom & Copperworks Distilling. (7324 NE 175th Street, Kenmore).

Course: Timed, marked out-and-back route on the Burke-Gilman Trail, heading east toward Bothell

 

8:00 AM - 11:00 AM        

8:00 AM | Packet Pickup Begins  
8:45 AM - 9:00 AM | Launch 10K & Kid Run 
9:00 AM - 9:15 AM | 5K Line Up & Run/Walk Begins   
10:15 AM - 11:00 AM | Finisher Awards and Community Celebration

 

Event Details

Giveaway, Medals & More
All registered participants will receive a commemorative medal, and those who register by September 1 are guaranteed an event giveaway. After September 1, giveaways will be available while supplies last.

Giveaway: Guaranteed with registration by September 1; limited quantities thereafter

Medals: Awarded to all registered race participants

Pets Welcome: Leashed pets, pet strollers, or wagons are welcome on the course. Please ensure pets remain on a short leash and that owners clean up after their animals.

Parking: Parking is available on nearby streets and at the Kenmore Park & Ride, which offers crosswalk access at the traffic light for convenient entry to the event.

 

Bib Pick-Up Week of Race:

Wednesday - Thursday @ Bothell Kenmore Chamber Office (10:00 AM - 2:00 PM)
Friday @ launch location 4:00 PM - 7:00 PM
Day of Event 8:00 AM

name: One Step Closer
description:
What do you get when you take Orca Running and mix it with Evergreen Trail!? Welcome to One Step Closer. An exciting summer endurance event created by Orca Running AND Evergreen Trail Runs. Part whale, part trail-and loopy. Held in the one and only Lincoln Park, this race is going to be THE summer endurance event you won’t want to miss.

Course: Loops at Lincoln Park. Amazingly diverse for its size, this race experience has a bit of everything. Runners will take on a 2 mile course loop, and complete the loop as many times as they can during their selected time period: 18 hours, 12 hours, 6 hours, or 3 hours. All runners will finish together at 11:00pm with a finish line party! 

Check out all the details on our website!

description:
The Orca Half is a half marathon along the shores of West Seattle, starting at Lincoln Park and finishing at Don Armeni Boat Launch. The half course is point to point, with two small out and back sections in the beginning and a longer one towards the end.  The 8-miler course is point to point, with two small out and back sections in the beginning. 

See all of race details on our website here!

name: Palouse to Cascades Marathon+ Relay
description:
Experience the beauty and spirit of Kittitas County as you run through breathtaking natural landscapes and charming small towns along the historic Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail. This unique course follows the former Milwaukee Road railroad corridor—offering runners an unforgettable journey through tunnels, bridges, and scenic backcountry terrain. 

A Washington State Discovery Pass is required.

Teams of four (male, female, or co-ed) will each tackle a leg of the race, combining endurance, teamwork, and adventure in a celebration of outdoor fitness.  

As noted in The Financial Times article, “The Rise of the Relay Marathon,” “Relays are the perfect Venn diagram of fitness trends: a mix of ultra-marathoning, trail running, and the great outdoors.” Come be part of this exciting trend—right here in the heart of Washington!

Important Rules & Safety Notes:

Zero Tolerance Policy: Absolutely no consumption of alcohol or drugs on the course. Any team found in violation will be immediately disqualified and banned from future events.

Vehicle Restrictions: No vehicles wider than 80 inches or longer than 20 feet are allowed. Motorhomes, buses, and limousines are strictly prohibited for all teams and support personnel.  Feel free to decorate your support vehicle.  However, please refrain from the use of foul or overly suggestive language for decorations.  Have fun but please use good judgement and be respectful.

Obey State Laws & Volunteers:  Each team member must obey all Washington State Laws and event volunteers.  The Trail crosses 2 major highways.

No dogs or bicycles:  Absolutely no dogs or bicycle are allowed on the Trail for this event.

name: Port Angeles Turkey Trot
description:
Port Angeles Turkey Trot – Run, Walk, and Gobble!
Kick off your Thanksgiving with a fun and festive tradition for all ages! Run the Peninsula is delighted to host this year’s Port Angeles Turkey Trot, offering both 5K and 10K options for runners, walkers, friends, and families.
Proceeds supports the Port Angeles Food Bank, so you’re doing good while feeling great!
  • $200+ Donation Gives you a FREE Entry to the 5K or 10K Port Angeles Turkey Trot
  • $100 Donation Gives you a $20 off Entry to the 5K or 10K Port Angeles Turkey Trot
  • $50 Donation Give you $10 off Entry to the 5K or 10K Port Angeles Turkey Trot
Event Details:
Date: Thanksgiving Morning - Thursday, November 27th
Time: Race starts at 9:00 AM
Location: Hollywood Beach, Port Angeles
Distances: 5K & 10K — both are out-and-back courses on the Olympic Discovery Trail
Who Can Join: All ages and paces welcome—strollers and festive outfits encouraged!
Your Registration Includes:
  • Commemorative Port Angeles Turkey Trot Medal
  • Long-sleeve race t-shirt
  • Plenty of Thanksgiving fun and good cheer!
Gather your flock and make memories before the feast—come trot with us at Hollywood Beach!
Bag Check:
Bring your own bag or use one of ours! Write your bib number on it, drop it before the race, and pick it up afterward with ease.
This Event is produced by the Port Angeles Marathon Association the same Non-Profit 501c3 Organization that puts on the North Olympic Discovery Marathon and the Run the Peninsula Series. 
For questions please click on the question box below or call 585-451-0014

name: Quilcene Oyster Races
description:
Come and run or walk our Half Marathon, 10K, and 5K races in peaceful Quilcene on the beautiful Olympic Peninsula!

The surroundings include woodlands, water, and mountains. All race proceeds benefit Quilcene-Brinnon Dollars for Scholars, which provides scholarships to high school seniors, recent graduates, and teachers to assist with their post-secondary/continuing education.

All Half Marathon, 10K and 5K events are USATF Certified and Sanctioned. Our Duo events are for participants paired with riders in jogging chairs/strollers (or for our easy 5K, even baby strollers and wagons!). All riders register for free!

The races begin and end at Worthington Park, site of the recently restored Victorian-era Worthington Mansion. Great scenery, awesome volunteers, and support for good causes make this a "can't-miss" event!

Registration includes:
  • A commemorative Finisher Medal
  • One serving of local oysters after the race
  • One local craft beer after the race (21 and over)
  • Free open house at Worthington Mansion
  • Lots of fun!

name: Rainier to Ruston
description:
NEW START: Carbonado.
The race start is on AP Tubbs Road East.
Take Highway 165 towards Carbonado.
Turn right on Wilkeson Carbonado Road E.
Just after passing the cemetery, turn right on AP Tubbs Road E.
The race start is 1/4 mile on the right.

New Route and Legs on the Website!

Who doesn’t love to cram into a vehicle in the wee early morning hours with run gear, snacks, and your friends in anticipation of the van becoming more rancid as the day goes on? (BIG TIP! Ziploc bags for sweaty clothes. Adventures await you as you climb into the vehicle like clowns at the circus.

Teams of 2, 3, 4, or 6 runners will compete to win the coveted RR spikes for each award category. What’s better than that? EVERYONE is a winner with the reward of a craft beer garden and finish line food at the finish line. Look up to see the stunner of Mount Rainier. Get a mug shot with our famous bell stand with that gem in the background. Feel free to lie down and rehash stories of the epic relay adventure that started from the base of Mount Rainier to the cool, grassy waterfront of Tacoma, where you are now resting. Put your feet up. You deserve it.

name: Redmond Harvest Half Marathon
description: Harvest the fruits of your training at the Redmond Harvest Half Marathon, to be held Labor Day Monday (September 7, 2026)! Starting from Redmond’s Marymoor Park, the Harvest Half is a fast, flat out-and-back half-marathon that goes west out of Marymoor Park and north on the Sammamish River Trail before returning to the start. Whether this is your first half-marathon, or you are experienced with this distance, this 13.1-mile course will give you an opportunity for your running goals to come to fruition. Come support a local race put on by Lake Sammamish Run Club and Seattle United Runners and finish your summer with a bang.

name: Reflection Run
description:
REFLECTION RUN HAS RAISED ALMOST $60,000 THANKS TO YOU!

The 11th Annual Reflection Run will honor the brave men and women who have or are currently serving in our Armed Forces and remember those who have given the ultimate sacrifice fighting for our freedom. The Half Marathon, 10K & 5K running and walking courses will travel along the mighty Columbia River with views of Mt. Hood and the Gorge. The routes will be lined with local Hero Posters of those who have given the ultimate sacrifice, and the event will benefit various Northwest Battle Buddies & various Military Organizations and Non-profits.

 

Veterans and those actively serving race Reflection Run for FREE. It’s our way of thanking you for your service. Email registration@whyracingevents.com with your Military service details and we will send you a comp code so you can register.

 

After your run or walk on the beautiful Washougal trail, we will enjoy food and drink and share race stories and meet Veterans or those currently serving in the Armed Forces so we can personally thank them for their service.

The Half Marathon, 10K & 5K running and walking courses will travel along the mighty Columbia River with views of Mt. Hood and the Gorge. The routes will be lined with local Hero Posters of those who have given the ultimate sacrifice, and the event will benefit various Northwest Battle Buddies & various Military Organizations and Non-profits.

 

Veterans and those actively serving race Reflection Run for FREE. It’s our way of thanking you for your service. Email registration@whyracingevents.com with your Military service details and we will send you a comp code so you can register.

 

After your run or walk on the beautiful Washougal trail, we will enjoy food and drink and share race stories and meet Veterans or those currently serving in the Armed Forces so we can personally thank them for their service.

name: Resolution Run
description:
Double the course and double the fun! Welcome to the 4th Annual Resolution Run in La Center, Washington as it continues to be a fundraiser for the La Center High School Volleyball program. We brought together all of our favorite things, a challenging course to kickup your New Year training program, trails and pathways along a very scenic course, and a good old-fashioned breakfast. You will start and finish at La Center High School - one loop for the 5K and a slightly different course for the 10K to really kick up the resolution challenge a notch. After your race, join us in the cafeteria for an all you can eat pancake and sausage with your $10 donation supporting the La Center High School Volleyball program. An awards ceremony for the overall top 3 finishers and age group winners will be provided.  There will be fun for all!!

name: Resolution Run 5K and Polar Bear Dive - 2026
description:
The Resolution Run is a 5K run/walk and finish festival celebrating the start of the New Year, with an optional Polar Plunge into Lake Washington.

Free chili, hot chocolate, apple cider! ★ Over 60 divisional prizes! ★ Long sleeve shirt or medal! ★ Free kids dash! ★ Beer garden (21+) if New Years Eve wasn’t enough!

Polar PLUNGE
The optional Polar Bear Dive into Lake Washington is located just before the finish line. About 60% of runners chose the Polar Bear Dive. We will have two heated gender specific changing room tents onsite for participants to change into dry clothes. Polar plunge and “dry” 5k results scored separately.

name: Rhinos 5K Fun Run
description:
The Rhinos 5K is an out-and-back fun run on the Lowell Riverfront Trail in Everett, WA. It starts and ends at Lowell Riverfront Park and offers gorgeous views along the Snohomish River.

On race day, packet pickup will begin at 9AM and end at 10:20AM at the Start Line in Lowell Riverfront Park. The race will begin at 10:30AM and parking is free.

Sign up now to get your race T-shirt and finisher medal on the day of the race! Check out this year's designs on the race website. Note that we cannot guarantee T-shirt sizes after 5pm on April 17th, but we'll do our best!

Walkers and runners are all welcome with a reduced price for kids. All proceeds go directly to supporting the Snohomish County Rhinos Rugby Team!

name: Richland RunFest 2026
description:
RICHLAND RUNFEST 2026 is presented by 3 Rivers Road Runners (3RRR)

DISTANCES:

  • Half Marathon, 10K and 5K (both in person and virtual options)
  • There will be a medal for each race (and they will fit together to make one big medal if you do all 3!!!)
  • You can register for one in person option and then the other distances virtually or all 3 races virtually to obtain all three medals that will fit together to make one cool medal.
  • Did I mention--Do all 3 races and you get 3 medals that go together to get one big medal--you have 3 weeks to complete the virtual options PRIOR to the in person race date and 1 week AFTER the in person race date and you get a discount.

DATES:

  • In Person Race: Saturday, February 28, 2026 
  • Virtual Race Window:  Friday February 6, 2026 to Friday, March 6, 2026 at 11:59 pm.

TIMES:

  • Half Marathon will start at 8:30am
  • 10K and 5K will start at 8:45am
  • ALL race courses close at 12:30 PM.

WHERE:  

  • Richland, WA
  • Start and Finish will be at Columbia Point Marina Park 
  • Use the address of 660 Columbia Point Drive, Richland WA 99354 for GPS directions.

FACEBOOK

  • Please like us on Facebook for updates and inspiration: www.facebook.com/richlandrunfest.
  • This year we have a running group and training plan (both beginner and intermediate/advanced) for ALL distances: the half marathon, 10K and 5K.  See Facebook for details or see the running group and training plan section.

REGISTRATION:

 

RACE DISTANCE

Until 11/16/2025

11/17/2025 to 12/31/2025

1/1/2026 to 1/31/2026

2/1/2026 to 2/28/2026**

 

Half Marathon

$75

 

10K

5K
